beats.text: Welcome to the ten-minute rapid review of innate immunity. We cover the top pearls and traps from all six modules, then build one master map.
beats.no_facts_reason: Intro and orientation; no factual claim.
beats.visual: Title card; six module tiles appear.

beats.text: Keep one rule in mind: the lost function predicts the disease. Lose an early classical component, and you often get lupus. Lose C3: pyogenic infections. Lose C5 to C9: Neisseria.
beats.visual: Rule written; three knock-out arrows to SLE, pyogenic, Neisseria.

beats.text: Module 1. Innate receptors are germline-encoded and nonclonal, with fewer than 100 types. Innate memory is limited.
beats.visual: M1 header; innate vs adaptive two-column compare.

beats.text: Three phases: immediate innate, zero to four hours. Early induced innate, four to ninety-six hours. Adaptive, after ninety-six hours.
beats.visual: Timeline arrow 0–4 h, 4–96 h, >96 h.

beats.text: Barriers come first: keratin, tight junctions, mucus and cilia. Paneth cells make alpha-defensins. LL-37 neutralizes LPS. In cystic fibrosis, thick mucus leads to lung infections.
beats.say: Barriers come first: keratin, tight junctions, mucus and cilia. Paneth cells make alpha-defensins. L L 37 neutralizes L P S. In cystic fibrosis, thick mucus leads to lung infections.
beats.visual: Barrier wall with labels; CF in pink.

beats.text: Trap: lysozyme works better on Gram-positive bacteria. In Gram-negatives, LPS covers the peptidoglycan.
beats.say: Trap: lysozyme works better on Gram-positive bacteria. In Gram-negatives, L P S covers the peptidoglycan.
beats.visual: Gram+ vs Gram− wall sketch; lysozyme hits Gram+.

beats.text: TNF, IL-1 and IL-6 cause fever, leukocytosis and acute-phase proteins. CRP can rise 1000-fold.
beats.say: T N F, I L 1 and I L 6 cause fever, leukocytosis and acute-phase proteins. C R P can rise 1000-fold.
beats.visual: Three cytokine boxes → fever, leukocytosis, CRP ×1000.

beats.text: TNF mediates much of septic shock. But trap: anti-TNF gave no benefit in sepsis trials, and TNF blockade can reactivate tuberculosis.
beats.say: T N F mediates much of septic shock. But trap: anti-T N F gave no benefit in sepsis trials, and T N F blockade can reactivate tuberculosis.
beats.visual: TNF → septic shock; anti-TNF crossed out for sepsis; TB warning.

beats.text: For allergy: epithelial IL-25, IL-33 and TSLP drive ILC2s, Th2 cells and mast cells. IL-33 is an alarmin.
beats.say: For allergy: epithelial I L 25, I L 33 and T S L P drive I L C 2s, T h 2 cells and mast cells. I L 33 is an alarmin.
beats.visual: Epithelium releases IL-25, IL-33, TSLP → ILC2, Th2, mast cell.

beats.text: Module 2, the cells. Neutrophils are the most abundant white cells, and they arrive first. Azurophilic granules hold myeloperoxidase and defensins. They also cast NETs.
beats.say: Module 2, the cells. Neutrophils are the most abundant white cells, and they arrive first. Azurophilic granules hold myeloperoxidase and defensins. They also cast nets.
beats.visual: M2 header; neutrophil cell with granules and NET strands.

beats.text: Abbas says most tissue macrophages are fetal-derived and self-renew. Janeway says they come from monocytes. CD47 binding SIRP-alpha is the don't-eat-me signal.
beats.say: Abbas says most tissue macrophages are fetal-derived and self-renew. Janeway says they come from monocytes. C D 47 binding SIRP-alpha is the don't-eat-me signal.
beats.visual: Macrophage; Abbas vs Janeway note; CD47–SIRPα handshake.

beats.text: Plasmacytoid DCs are the major type I interferon source. cDC1 cells cross-present to CD8 T cells.
beats.say: Plasmacytoid D Cs are the major type I interferon source. c D C 1 cells cross-present to C D 8 T cells.
beats.visual: Two DC boxes: pDC → type I IFN; cDC1 → CD8+ T cell.

beats.text: NK cells are CD56 positive, CD3 negative. Low MHC class I removes inhibition: missing self. CD16 binds IgG for ADCC.
beats.say: NK cells are C D 56 positive, C D 3 negative. Low M H C class I removes inhibition: missing self. C D 16 binds I g G for A D C C.
beats.visual: NK balance: inhibition vs activation; missing self tips balance.

beats.text: NK deficiency, for example GATA2 or CD16, gives severe herpesvirus and papillomavirus infections.
beats.say: NK deficiency, for example GATA 2 or C D 16, gives severe herpesvirus and papillomavirus infections.
beats.visual: NK cell struck out → herpesvirus, papillomavirus.

beats.text: Trap: tryptase, not histamine, marks mast cell activation. C3a, C5a and MRGPRX2 activate mast cells without IgE.
beats.say: Trap: tryptase, not histamine, marks mast cell activation. C 3 a, C 5 a and M R G P R X 2 activate mast cells without I g E.
beats.visual: Mast cell; tryptase in yellow, histamine struck; non-IgE triggers.

beats.text: Trap: eosinophils have very low FcεRI without a signalling chain. IL-5 is their key cytokine. Galectin-10 forms Charcot-Leyden crystals.
beats.say: Trap: eosinophils have very low F c epsilon R 1 without a signalling chain. I L 5 is their key cytokine. Galectin-10 forms Charcot-Leyden crystals.
beats.visual: Eosinophil; IL-5 arrow; Charcot-Leyden crystal.

beats.text: Module 3, sensing. Location predicts the ligand. Surface TLRs 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6 see microbial walls. Endosomal TLRs 3, 7, 8 and 9 see nucleic acids.
beats.say: Module 3, sensing. Location predicts the ligand. Surface T L Rs 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6 see microbial walls. Endosomal T L Rs 3, 7, 8 and 9 see nucleic acids.
beats.visual: M3 header; cell with surface TLRs and endosome TLRs.

beats.text: LPS binds TLR4, with MD2 and CD14. Flagellin binds TLR5. Double-stranded RNA binds TLR3. CpG DNA binds TLR9.
beats.say: L P S binds T L R 4, with M D 2 and C D 14. Flagellin binds T L R 5. Double-stranded RNA binds T L R 3. C p G DNA binds T L R 9.
beats.visual: Ligand → TLR matching lines.

beats.text: Classic trap: TLR3 is the only TLR without MyD88. Only TLR3 and TLR4 use TRIF, so TLR4 uses both.
beats.say: Classic trap: T L R 3 is the only T L R without My D 88. Only T L R 3 and T L R 4 use trif, so T L R 4 uses both.
beats.visual: MyD88 vs TRIF table; TLR3 TRIF only; TLR4 both.

beats.text: MyD88 or IRAK4 deficiency: early invasive pneumococcal infection with no fever, a cold infection. TLR3, UNC93B or TRIF defects: herpes simplex encephalitis.
beats.say: My D 88 or IRAK 4 deficiency: early invasive pneumococcal infection with no fever, a cold infection. T L R 3, U N C 93 B or trif defects: herpes simplex encephalitis.
beats.visual: Two clue cards: cold pneumococcus; HSV encephalitis.

beats.text: NLRP3 senses urate crystals, ATP and potassium efflux. Caspase-1 cleaves pro-IL-1β and IL-18. Gasdermin D pores cause pyroptosis, in macrophages and DCs, but not neutrophils.
beats.say: N L R P 3 senses urate crystals, ATP and potassium efflux. Caspase-1 cleaves pro-I L 1 beta and I L 18. Gasdermin D pores cause pyroptosis, in macrophages and D Cs, but not neutrophils.
beats.visual: Inflammasome chain NLRP3 → caspase-1 → IL-1β; pyroptosis: neutrophil crossed.

beats.text: NLRP3 gain of function causes CAPS: FCAS with cold-induced fever and urticarial rash, and Muckle-Wells with deafness. Abbas reports that IL-1 antagonists work.
beats.say: N L R P 3 gain of function causes caps: F C A S with cold-induced fever and urticarial rash, and Muckle-Wells with deafness. Abbas reports that I L 1 antagonists work.
beats.visual: NLRP3 gain → CAPS → FCAS / Muckle-Wells; IL-1 block in orange.

beats.text: Trap: weak NOD2 variants raise Crohn's disease risk. NOD2 gain of function causes Blau syndrome.
beats.say: Trap: weak nod 2 variants raise Crohn's disease risk. nod 2 gain of function causes Blau syndrome.
beats.visual: NOD2 dial: weak → Crohn's; gain → Blau.

beats.text: Module 4, phagocytes. Recruitment runs: selectin rolling on sialyl Lewis X, integrin activation, firm arrest, transmigration.
beats.visual: M4 header; vessel with rolling → activation → arrest → transmigration.

beats.text: LAD-1, a CD18 defect: leukocytosis, no pus, poor wound healing. LAD-2: no sialyl Lewis X, Bombay blood group. LAD-3: bleeding with normal platelets.
beats.say: L A D 1, a C D 18 defect: leukocytosis, no pus, poor wound healing. L A D 2: no sialyl Lewis X, Bombay blood group. L A D 3: bleeding with normal platelets.
beats.visual: LAD-1/2/3 cards pinned to steps.

beats.text: Trap: LAD means leukocytosis in blood but no pus in tissue. Do not confuse it with severe congenital neutropenia, below 0.5 times 10 to the 9 per litre.
beats.say: Trap: L A D means leukocytosis in blood but no pus in tissue. Do not confuse it with severe congenital neutropenia, below 0.5 times 10 to the 9 per litre.
beats.visual: Blood full of cells vs tissue empty; SCN contrast.

beats.text: Respiratory burst: NADPH oxidase makes superoxide, which becomes hydrogen peroxide. Myeloperoxidase then makes hypohalous acid.
beats.say: Respiratory burst: N A D P H oxidase makes superoxide, which becomes hydrogen peroxide. Myeloperoxidase then makes hypohalous acid.
beats.visual: Chain O₂ → superoxide → H₂O₂ → HOCl with enzymes.

beats.text: CGD breaks the oxidase; two-thirds is X-linked gp91. Expect catalase-positive Staphylococcus, granulomas, and Aspergillus, the leading cause of death. MPO deficiency is milder.
beats.say: CGD breaks the oxidase; two-thirds is X-linked G P 91. Expect catalase-positive Staphylococcus, granulomas, and Aspergillus, the leading cause of death. M P O deficiency is milder.
beats.visual: Oxidase struck → CGD clue card; MPO block milder.

beats.text: Chédiak-Higashi, from LYST mutations: partial albinism, silver hair, giant lysosomes, weak NK cells.
beats.say: Chédiak-Higashi, from list mutations: partial albinism, silver hair, giant lysosomes, weak NK cells.
beats.visual: CHS card: LYST, albinism, silver hair, giant lysosomes.

beats.text: Disseminated BCG or Salmonella means MSMD: the IL-12 and IFN-γ axis fails.
beats.say: Disseminated B C G or Salmonella means M S M D: the I L 12 and interferon gamma axis fails.
beats.visual: IL-12 ⇄ IFN-γ loop between macrophage and NK/T; break → MSMD.

beats.text: Module 5, complement. C3 cleavage is central. Classical and lectin pathways share the C3 convertase C4b2a. The alternative pathway uses C3bBb.
beats.say: Module 5, complement. C3 cleavage is central. Classical and lectin pathways share the C3 convertase C 4 b 2 a. The alternative pathway uses C 3 b, B b.
beats.visual: Three pathways funnel into C3 → C3a + C3b.

beats.text: Trap: for C2, the larger bound fragment is C2a. Factor D circulates active. Properdin stabilizes C3bBb.
beats.say: Trap: for C2, the larger bound fragment is C 2 a. Factor D circulates active. Properdin stabilizes C 3 b, B b.
beats.visual: C2 → C2a (bound, big) + C2b; factor D, properdin tags.

beats.text: Only antigen-bound antibody activates C1. IgM beats IgG; IgG1 and IgG3 are best, and IgG4 does not activate complement.
beats.say: Only antigen-bound antibody activates C1. I g M beats I g G; I g G 1 and I g G 3 are best, and I g G 4 does not activate complement.
beats.visual: Ranking ladder IgM > IgG1/IgG3 > IgG4 ✗.

beats.text: C5a is the most potent anaphylatoxin, and degranulates mast cells without IgE. The membrane attack complex lets water in, and the cell bursts.
beats.say: C 5 a is the most potent anaphylatoxin, and degranulates mast cells without I g E. The membrane attack complex lets water in, and the cell bursts.
beats.visual: C5a > C3a bar; MAC pore with water entering.

beats.text: The brakes. Factor H regulates only the alternative pathway. C4BP binds C4b. DAF dissociates both C3 convertases. CD59 blocks C9.
beats.say: The brakes. Factor H regulates only the alternative pathway. C 4 B P binds C 4 b. D A F dissociates both C3 convertases. C D 59 blocks C9.
beats.visual: Four regulator labels attach to their targets.

beats.text: Module 6. C1q, C2 or C4 deficiency gives lupus in over half; C2 deficiency is the most common. C3 or factor I deficiency gives pyogenic infections.
beats.say: Module 6. C 1 q, C2 or C4 deficiency gives lupus in over half; C2 deficiency is the most common. C3 or factor I deficiency gives pyogenic infections.
beats.visual: M6 header; knock-out table rows 1–2.

beats.text: C5 to C9, properdin or factor D deficiency gives Neisseria. Properdin deficiency is X-linked. MBL deficiency is mild.
beats.say: C5 to C9, properdin or factor D deficiency gives Neisseria. Properdin deficiency is X-linked. M B L deficiency is mild.
beats.visual: Knock-out rows 3–4: Neisseria; MBL mild.

beats.text: Factor H or MCP mutations cause atypical HUS. PNH lacks CD59 and DAF. Trap: the PIG-A mutation in PNH is somatic, not inherited.
beats.say: Factor H or M C P mutations cause atypical H U S. P N H lacks C D 59 and D A F. Trap: the pig A mutation in P N H is somatic, not inherited.
beats.visual: Rows: aHUS; PNH with 'somatic' stamp.

beats.text: Hereditary angioedema is autosomal dominant C1 inhibitor deficiency, and bradykinin causes the swelling. Clues: abdominal attacks, no wheals, no response to antihistamines.
beats.visual: Bradykinin swelling; clue list; antihistamine struck out.

beats.text: The 2017 guideline says: test C1 inhibitor function, protein, and C4. HAE type 1: low function, low protein. Type 2: low function, normal or high protein.
beats.say: The 2017 guideline says: test C1 inhibitor function, protein, and C4. H A E type 1: low function, low protein. Type 2: low function, normal or high protein.
beats.visual: Lab table columns: function, protein, C4; HAE-1, HAE-2 rows.

beats.text: Acquired angioedema starts later, with lymphoma or MGUS, and C1q is low in 75 percent. ACE inhibitor angioedema has normal C1 inhibitor.
beats.say: Acquired angioedema starts later, with lymphoma or M G U S, and C 1 q is low in 75 percent. A C E inhibitor angioedema has normal C1 inhibitor.
beats.visual: Lab table adds AAE row (C1q low) and ACEI row.

beats.text: HAE traps. C3 and CH50 are normal. Normal C1 inhibitor does not exclude HAE. C4 is not useful below 12 months. Wheals do not exclude HAE.
beats.say: H A E traps. C3 and C H 50 are normal. Normal C1 inhibitor does not exclude H A E. C4 is not useful below 12 months. Wheals do not exclude H A E.
beats.visual: Four trap cards flip in.

beats.text: Treatment follows the 2017 guideline; check the current one. Treat attacks early with C1 inhibitor, ecallantide or icatibant, not tranexamic acid or androgens.
beats.visual: Orange drug box with 'check current guideline' banner.

beats.text: For long-term prophylaxis, C1 inhibitor is first line, androgens second. Carry medication for two attacks. Avoid ACE inhibitors.
beats.say: For long-term prophylaxis, C1 inhibitor is first line, androgens second. Carry medication for two attacks. Avoid A C E inhibitors.
beats.visual: LTP ladder; 2 attack kits; ACE inhibitor crossed.

beats.text: Now the master map. Barriers fail in cystic fibrosis. Sensing fails in cold infections, herpes encephalitis and CAPS. Cells fail in severe congenital neutropenia.
beats.say: Now the master map. Barriers fail in cystic fibrosis. Sensing fails in cold infections, herpes encephalitis and caps. Cells fail in severe congenital neutropenia.
beats.visual: D21 rows 1–3 build: stage, players, disease.

beats.text: Effector mechanisms: phagocytosis fails in LAD, CGD and Chédiak-Higashi. Complement: lupus, Neisseria, HAE, PNH. Inflammation: septic shock, IL-1 excess. NK cells: herpesviruses.
beats.say: Effector mechanisms: phagocytosis fails in L A D, CGD and Chédiak-Higashi. Complement: lupus, Neisseria, H A E, P N H. Inflammation: septic shock, I L 1 excess. NK cells: herpesviruses.
beats.visual: D21 row 4 with four sub-rows.

beats.text: Last, the link to adaptive immunity. Antigen is signal 1. Innate responses give signal 2: costimulators like CD80 and CD86, cytokines and complement products. Failure here: MSMD.
beats.say: Last, the link to adaptive immunity. Antigen is signal 1. Innate responses give signal 2: costimulators like C D 80 and C D 86, cytokines and complement products. Failure here: M S M D.
beats.visual: D21 row 5; whole map visible.

beats.text: Five things to remember. Innate receptors are germline-encoded. Location predicts the ligand. Lost function predicts disease. HAE is bradykinin-mediated. Innate immunity gives signal 2.
beats.say: Five things to remember. Innate receptors are germline-encoded. Location predicts the ligand. Lost function predicts disease. H A E is bradykinin-mediated. Innate immunity gives signal 2.
beats.visual: Five numbered lines appear one by one.

beats.text: One last trap: TLR3 is the only TLR without MyD88. Review the master map before the exam. Good luck!
beats.say: One last trap: T L R 3 is the only T L R without My D 88. Review the master map before the exam. Good luck!
beats.visual: Trap card, then full D21 map returns as the closing frame.
